q: Today, we received a very lengthy message from the daycare director talking about how concerning the amount of sleep he is getting there is for his age, how he cries pretty much all day, and that he is not getting enough food. This is of course extremely heartbreaking to hear as a first time mom
cx: First-time mother of a 7-month-old who will not nap at daycare.

q: the message (and tone) really hurt my feelings and made me feel like I am failing as a mom. […] However, we know that he is fussy because he is overtired.
cx: Daycare blames hunger; she believes it is overtiredness.

q: They told us due to state regulations, they are not allowed to hold or rock him to sleep. So I imagine they are seeing sleepy cues and just laying him down.
cx: Why the baby who is rocked at home cannot nap at daycare.

q: My husband and I both feel that the whole “no holding/rocking” comment is an excuse for not being adequately staffed to give any additional time to a child that may need it to sleep
cx: Parents suspect understaffing behind the daycare's rule.

q: My wife has fed our baby to sleep pretty much every night since the baby was born 12 months ago. […] My wife understandably feels fed up and doesn't want to feel so trapped. She wants me to be able to put her to sleep.
cx: A father asked to take over bedtime from breastfeeding to sleep.

q: I tried last night (with a bed time routine of books, a warm bottle of milk and then trying to put her to sleep in the sling) and I'experienced a tantrum unlike anything I'm used to - screaming, sobbing, pushing me away
cx: His first attempt at bedtime without the breast.

q: I'm not looking for relationship advice, I'm looking for sleep advice or a consultant to use or some way to get her to sleep without the breast.
cx: Pre-empts relationship replies; open to paying a consultant.

q: She only started having a preference for me lately (i.e. going to me when mum is an option) and I'm kind of worried about her associating me with these very distressful evenings.
cx: The father's fear that taking over bedtime will cost him the bond.

q: I tried one evening of sleeptraining (conventional ferber method) when he was 5 months old. He screamed bloody murder for 1.5 hours. Going in to soothe him wasn't helping, he screamed even louder.
cx: Breastfeeding mother of a 9-month-old, now planning to try again on parental leave.

q: I thought I could just tough it out until he wanted to wean breastfeeding […] but I just can't. I really can't do it anymore, i've come to the conclusion that I will have to sleeptrain one way or another.
cx: She never wanted to sleep train; months of hourly nursing changed her mind.

q: But i think i may need to resort to this again if the "chair method" doesn't work when i'll try druing my parental leave (4 months starting next weekend). When do i even check in when trying ferber/full extinction?
cx: Her exact-steps question, with a backup method lined up.

q: I've tried keeping to sleep schedules, it doesn't seem to make much of a difference, at least not for getting him to actually sleep at night, or sleeping through the night.
cx: Same mother on schedules.

q: MIL always has a tendency to be the loudest while we’re trying to put her down for a nap or RIGHT after we get her to bed, which is when the noise wakes her immediately. This leads to a really POd LO, because then she’s overtired.
cx: New mother living in her mother-in-law's basement with a two-week-old.

q: She will offer to watch LO so we can rest, but she doesn’t even attempt to let LO sleep, and just lets her stay up, which means we get a screaming, cranky baby after we get back up.
cx: Help from the grandmother that costs sleep.

q: the gentle conversations and reminders about at least attempting to adhere to schedules and noise levels at certain points seem to fall on deaf ears, then I am up sobbing with a baby attached to my breast for hours on end.
cx: Same mother on why talking to the mother-in-law has not worked.

q: Today was the first day I actually felt successful with her in a while, and all she needed was to not be kept up past her “wake window”
cx: A day with the mother-in-law out of the house.

q: Only 1 week after we were home, she asked if we were doing chores around the baby. I was so angry in the moment and thinking “we haven’t even gotten the chance because we can’t get her to sleep in the first place with the nonstop noise”.
cx: What the mother-in-law said a week after the birth.

q: I returned to work and 13 month old started daycare (3 days a week), he loves it - has a great time, very sociable and smiley. Except he doesn't nap well - they can get maybe 45 minutes out of him, tops.  He normally has a single 2.5 hour sleep at home.
cx: Parent back at work; daycare naps collapse and nights follow.

q: I'm exhausted and a zombie at work.  It has been 1.5 months and I can't see an end to this. The nights are seriously as disrupted as the newborn stage, except we have to function at work the next day regardless!
cx: Same parent, six weeks into daycare.

q: He recently became sick and had an entire week off where his sleep got better - but the second he went back, 40 minute nap and I'm sending him to daycare today with only 8 hours' night sleep.
cx: A week at home fixed sleep; daycare undid it at once.

q: my husband and I have sacrificed a lot to have in-home childcare […] However, baby WILL NOT nap with her. Our baby sleeps okay in the bassinet during the night but during the day she usually contact naps on either me or her dad.
cx: Parent working from home with a new nanny and a 15-week-old contact napper.

q: I found my daughter's crying SO hard that I think I am sabotaging their relationship by not letting her settle with the nanny. […] I set a 10 min timer and then go in to see if I can help.
cx: She interrupts the nanny's settling because she cannot bear the crying.

q: We've been trying to CIO but she won't fall back asleep even after an hour of crying and we are both begging for sleep so at that point I cave and breastfeed her back to sleep. We've tried Ferber and it just makes her even more upset.
cx: Breastfeeding mother of an almost 8-month-old with short daycare naps and 2-3 hourly wakes.

q: I don't have control over naps at daycare and she only sleeps 30 min - 45 min each nap. […] (3/3/4.5 wake windows currently) […] Is our last WW stretching to 4.5 hrs too long? Should we push up her bed time to 6?
cx: Same mother doing the wake-window arithmetic around a fixed daycare schedule.

q: I woke up at 10.30 AM to hear he putting her outside (1 hour or 30 minutes after the usual). I don't want to be too strict or rigid or ungrateful but I told him that it was too late. He told me it doesn't matter and to loosen up.
cx: Nordic parent of a 3.5-month-old; the partner ran the morning nap on a holiday.

q: if her routine is disrupted, she wakes up multiple times and needs extra consoling to stay asleep. Then I have to do it when I wake up. But maybe in the future I will let him deal with the consequences 😁
cx: Why the late nap matters to the parent who handles the fallout.

q: Please give it to me straight - am I being too strict or is my husband being too callous?
cx: The ask: settle the couple's argument about routine.

q: It’s been nearly 13months of me being the only one who gets my little one to sleep via the boob. My husband and I had a chat last night about him getting more involved
cx: Mother leaving the house for the night so the father handles wakings.

q: This usually ends in a lot of crying and I cave and go in, but we decided if I leave the house the two of them are going to have to make it work. I’m glad he’s willing to try it but I’m nervous as hell.
cx: Why she must physically leave for the handover to work.

q: I guess it’s never going to be perfect but we’ve got to try something different or nothing will change and dad will continue being on the outside.
cx: Same mother after reading replies.

q: Our 2,5 year old started kindergarten last week. Everything is great, but her scedule got moved an hour and now everything is fucked up.
cx: A sleep-trained toddler whose nap moved with a new kindergarten schedule.

q: I just did that. Put her down 19.40, it is 20.20 and she is still singing and talking 🙃 Gonna be a long day tomorrow.
cx: Same night, after trying the commenter's earlier bedtime.

q: she immediately retorts “I NEVER advocate for crying of any kind.” […] She responded “oh well NO judgement on you, I would just NEVER allow a baby to cry like that, I’m a HOLISTIC sleep coach, but whatever works best for YOU” (with a very patronising tone)
cx: A holistic sleep coach met at soft play reacts to the parent's story.

q: Like your friend has just said her baby cries for HOURS trying a non-CIO method so at what point does it cross the line from not crying to crying?
cx: The coach's friend had hours of crying with shush-pat.

q: my baby used to wake up every 30-60 minutes for MONTHS. We were dying until we got somewhere with CIO, and now with wave method she’s usually out before or just after first check in at 5 mins, and only wakes 2 times for feeds which is fine by me.
cx: Parent of a 9-month-old: CIO went backwards, then the wave method held.
